The call cap is the smaller of the per-call cap and what the stage budget leaves, a decimal USD string with six places; here the stage budget leaves 750000 micros and the per-call cap of 500000 binds. No model is called.

changed.description: One field: line 10.

cases.purpose: A field the template does not declare never enters the prompt: the prompt and its hash are those of the typed input alone (the same typed fields as prompt_from_typed_input), and the dropped name is reported. The stage budget leaves 250000 micros, below the per-call cap, so what it leaves caps the call.

status.source: reconciled cases; every expected value given alike by two blind independent implementations (docs/eksik-kaydi.md E161)

cases.purpose: The block's fields come from the ledger and imports.jsonl alone: the last cycle_start row's cycle_id; the last events decision row's decision (a later events row of another kind does not replace it); the seconds from the genesis row to the last cycle_start row; the cost rows of every cycle summed against the cap; one human touch per imports.jsonl row. The block in status.md hashes to the last status row's block_sha256: not edited.

changed.description: One field: imports.jsonl has a third row, a human touch that is not a transfer (imports_three.jsonl).

cases.purpose: A hand edit inside the block (the human touch count lowered): the sha256 of the block found in status.md is not the last recorded one, so the block is regenerated and a status_edited events row carries both hashes.

changed.description: One byte: the block as the referee wrote it (status.md).

cases.purpose: Only the bytes between the two marker lines are the block: an edit in the rest of status.md (the part docs.render owns) is not a block edit.

changed.description: One byte inside the block instead (status_edited.md).

cases.purpose: status.md has no block while the ledger records one: a deleted block is an edit, with no found hash.

changed.description: One field: the first cycle's ledger before any status row (ledger_first.jsonl); no block and none recorded is not an edit.

cases.purpose: The brake is engaged once the ledger's spend reaches the cap; the cost rows of every cycle count, not only the current cycle's.

changed.description: One byte: the cap is 3501.

cases.purpose: Every cycle appends a status row, so the ledger holds one per cycle: the recorded hash is the last status row's (cycle 2's block), not the first's. status.md holding the block cycle 2 wrote is not edited; cycle 1's row is history.

changed.description: One field: status.md holds cycle 1's block, the one the earlier status row records (status.md).

genesis.source: reconciled cases; every expected value given alike by two blind independent implementations (docs/eksik-kaydi.md E161)

cases.purpose: Every precondition read from the recorded API holds for the toy target. The toy is cut from main (25a:21): its base_sha is main's head as the API reports it, not the summary's targets[].base_sha, which differs here. The planned genesis row binds that base SHA, the last imports.jsonl row (its bytes, its referee tree and (A) result hashes), the last seed epoch, the bytes of policy.json, summary.json and the seed security ledger, that ledger's last row_hash, the recipe's RFC 8785 hash and the hash of the API responses it read.

changed.description: One byte of policy.json (policy_b.json).

cases.purpose: The copy target: its base_sha is the summary's targets[].base_sha (25a:21) and its main is not read; its Actions permission is read and enters the facts hash.

changed.description: One field: imports.jsonl has a newer last row (imports_next.jsonl).

cases.purpose: The recipe hash is of its RFC 8785 form: the same recipe with other key order and indentation gives the payload of the compact file (toy_genesis_row's).

changed.description: One field: limits.kos_wall_s is 601 (recipe_b.json, compact).

cases.purpose: The copy target's Actions are enabled: activation is a hard stop and no genesis row is planned.

cases.purpose: Six facts fail at once and each is named: the writer App is also installed on another repository, brain/state lacks non_fast_forward, brain/integration lacks pull_request and its required check is reported by another App, main's only restriction is a pull request rule asking no approving review, and the toy has a workflow (25a:20). The toy's main differs from the summary's base_sha too, which is no fault: the toy is cut from main.

changed.description: One field: the recorded API where every fact holds (api.json).

cases.purpose: The writer App may bypass the copy's brain/state ruleset (current_user_can_bypass pull_requests_only) and is exempt from main's, though main's update rule leaves it to bypass alone: each ruleset the rules of brain/state, brain/integration and main come from is read, and only never counts (25a:17-18, 01b:59-60). Both are named and activation stops.

changed.description: One field: the recorded API where the writer App bypasses no ruleset (api.json).
